verdict.text: f1 is fixed.
Each rclone listing now writes straight to its file with its own exit guard, and sorting happens in separate steps.
A new test rejects any rclone line that pipes with a single `|`.
The f2 allowlist is also in, with exit 5 and a test that pins it to the four durable buckets.
Two non-blocking items are left.
The docs do not mention exit 5 (f3).
And the brief says main was merged, but the staged tree only goes up to main before the observability merge, so landing will hit doc conflicts again (f4).
The code merges cleanly and the tests pass on the merged tree.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: pass pre_commit, pass cli_tests, pass r1, pass r2, stamp green 141a16ef1e7eb5a3eda8046f3154484cf3731a73e581b95dcdde3bbb4747af62.
restore-s3.hcl, read in full.
Both `lsf -R` listings redirect to /tmp/src-dirs and /tmp/dst-dirs with `|| exit 4` and `|| exit 3`, and `sort -o` runs after them.
The top-level prefix listing is `prefixes=$(rclone lsf ...) || exit 4`.
An assignment takes the status of its command substitution, so that guard works.
The later `echo "$prefixes" | grep` pipe has no rclone in it.
An unchecked `sort -o` failure would leave the files unsorted, and `comm` would then report false missing entries and exit 3.
That fails safe.
The case allowlist runs before any GCS access, and anything else exits 5.
test_no_rclone_output_is_piped: the regex looks for a single `|` on a line that contains rclone, outside a `#`.
It would catch `rclone lsf ... | sort > f || exit 4`, which is exactly the f1 shape, and `||` does not match it.
test_only_durable_buckets_are_restored pins the case arm to DURABLE_BUCKETS and to exit 5.
Base: `git diff --cached main` still shows main's observability work reversed (grafana/seaweedfs.json, test_observability_s3_clients.py, loki.hcl, tempo.hcl).
Comparing the staged tree with each main commit shows it matches main as of 64a54fa/88003ec, which is before 62b07a6.
I simulated a merge (commit-tree of the staged tree, then `git merge-tree` against main).
It reports conflicts only in .loop/ and .okf/ files.
The .tf, .hcl and test files merge cleanly.
`uv run --directory cli pytest` on the merged tree, extracted to scratch, gave 637 passed and 1 failed.
The failure is test_versions' `git grep`, which only fails because the scratch copy is not a git repo.
The header comment in restore-s3.hcl now lists exit codes 1 to 5 and the reason for not piping.
f1 (resolved): fixed in restore-s3.hcl as described under Checked, and test_no_rclone_output_is_piped guards it.
f2 (resolved): the case allowlist with exit 5, guarded by test_only_durable_buckets_are_restored.
f3 (docs, non-blocking): add a row for 5 to the exit-code table in docs/reference/gcs-backups.md, and add a step 0 that refuses a bucket that is not one of the four durable ones.
Add "5 not a durable bucket" to the exit-code sentence in .okf/components/gcs-backups.md, and also mention the SeaweedFS listing under 3 there, as the reference page does.

f4 (docs, non-blocking): merge current main (7593db6, which contains 62b07a6) before landing, and resolve the five .okf conflicts so that each page reflects both cutovers: Loki and Tempo on SeaweedFS from observability, and OpenViking, models and datalake from this ticket.
The code needs no change.
After the merge, seaweedfs.md still says "The cutover comes in later tickets".
Now that OpenViking and observability have both moved, that sentence should name what remains (registry, then MinIO removal).
